structured_output.summary:
I found no public CIFAR-100 result faster than your tip. The best public one is 75.29% in 8.11 s (futurebiohackers PR #3, SGD; it reports that Muon lost). E031 at 5.43 s is ahead of it, so the useful evidence comes from the CIFAR-10 Muon lineage. Treat its constants as untested priors: they were tuned on 10 classes at about 8 epochs.

Most actionable for the open hypotheses:
- **Weight averaging and LR floor (H4.5 / H4.5.1).** The CIFAR-10 champion Fable (1.83 s) decays the LR to a 5% floor. It then holds a low-LR tail with an EMA "lookahead" every 4 steps at decay 0.7, starting 8 steps before the decay ends. Separately, an EMA paper says averaging reduces how much LR decay is needed. Both fit your E035 lesson that averaging matters a lot here, which makes tuning the tail averaging a good source of margin.
- **Whitening-bias phase (H4.5.2).** Both the hiverge baseline (1.98 s) and Fable train the whitening bias for only 0.2 epochs. airbench94_muon keeps 3 epochs.
- **Muon constants (H4.2).** hiverge uses Muon lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655 at batch 1536 and 7.65 epochs; Fable uses ortho lr 0.2255. This backs E033's pointer toward lr ≈ 0.2. hiverge also adds two pieces your Muon lacks: a target-magnitude schedule that shrinks the update size from 0.50 to 0.079 over training, and periodic weight-norm renormalization.
- **Augmentation (H4.1).** hiverge keeps a mild brightness/contrast jitter (about 0.14/0.13) alongside translate 2 and label smoothing 0.09. That is a different kind of regularizer from cutout or translate, and it is untested here.
- **Batch size (H4.4).** Muon critical-batch-size theory says steps stop shrinking past a batch threshold. That fits E032 (3072 was step-limited). Every Muon CIFAR record sits at batch 1536-2000.
- **Resize and whole-run graph (H3.2.6 / H2.4.4).** Fulcrum measured the 24 px step at 0.575x a 32 px step with a whole-run CUDA graph, against about 0.65-0.82x with plain compile. The gap is 1.5-4 ms/step of eager optimizer and loader overhead. The 24/28/32 curriculum lost time without the whole-run graph. Fable still trains two-thirds of its epochs below 32 px, but on CIFAR-10. Fulcrum also found that EMA and global max pooling did not make the net more robust to low resolution.
- **Muon cost.** Gram Newton-Schulz would cut the FLOPs of your 704×6336 Newton-Schulz step by about 29%. That is my estimate, roughly 0.05 s per run, and it needs fp16 plus restarts to stay stable. Turbo-Muon gave only 0.8% on the CIFAR-10 speedrun.
- **Rules caution.** The LessWrong audit lists Fable's gaming: augmentation precomputed outside the timed region, picking fast machines, and a GPU cooldown. All three are illegal under RULES.md and must not be copied. The same audit says the other models' main gain was tuning the epoch count down.

findings.claim: Fable champion (CIFAR-10, 94%): widths 64/256/256, batch 1536, 8.875 train epochs with linear decay over 8.5 epochs to lr_floor 0.05 of peak, then a low-LR 'stabilization tail with lookahead-style weight EMA' (ema_start_before 8 steps before decay end, ema_every 4, ema_decay 0.7). Ortho (Muon) lr 0.2255, SGD momentum 0.825 nesterov, bias_lr 0.0573, head_lr 0.5415, label smoothing 0.09, translate 2 px plus brightness/contrast jitter, whiten_bias_epochs 0.2, res_schedule by epoch [24,24,24,28,28,28,32,32,32] (bilinear downsample in the compiled step), global max pool, NS 3 iterations (3.4576, -4.7391, 2.0843), fp16, whole-run CUDA graph.
findings.relevance: Gives concrete settings for an LR floor + EMA tail, a 0.2-epoch whitening-bias phase, Muon lr near 0.22 and global pooling. All are open or unmeasured on the arena tip. Note the averaging here is a short EMA tail, not whole-run Lookahead.

findings.claim: hiverge baseline (previous CIFAR-10 SOTA, 1.98 s): Muon lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, nesterov; batch 1536; ~7.65 epochs; linear warmdown with no warmup; whitening bias trained only for the first ceil(0.2*len(loader)) steps; translate 2 reflect, alternating flip, brightness 0.14 / contrast 0.13 jitter; LS 0.09; no EMA/Lookahead. Its Muon renormalizes weights to norm sqrt(rows) every norm_freq = 2+int(15*progress) steps, and orthogonalized updates are scaled to a target magnitude decaying linearly from 0.5012 to 0.0786 over training.
findings.relevance: Independent second data point for Muon lr ~0.2 (E033: 0.32 hurt, 0.2 untested) and a 0.2-epoch whiten-bias phase. Also shows two Muon features the arena likely lacks: a scheduled update magnitude and weight-norm projection. Color jitter is a regularizer the arena has not tried.

findings.claim: airbench94_muon: batch 2000, 8 epochs, Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 / nesterov, NS 3 steps (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315), bias_lr 0.053, head_lr 0.67, SGD momentum 0.85, wd 2e-6*batch, LS 0.2, no warmup, linear decay, whiten_bias trained for 3 epochs, BN momentum 0.6, widths 64/256/256, no Lookahead/EMA, TTA level 2.
findings.relevance: The arena's Muon constants come from here. This recipe has no Lookahead, while the arena found Lookahead worth 0.81 pp (E035). It also uses no warmup and keeps whiten_bias at 3 epochs, which later records (hiverge, Fable) cut to 0.2.

findings.claim: Relative to a 32 px step, the measured step cost is 0.575x at 24 px and 0.774x at 28 px with a whole-run CUDA graph (theory 0.562 / 0.766). Plain torch.compile gives 0.82x charged (~0.65x steady) at 24 px. A whole-run graph removed ~1.5-4 ms/step of eager optimizer/loader overhead. The same 24/28/32 curriculum LOST time under plain compile. Bilinear downsampling of the full 32 px crop cut the 24->28 accuracy penalty from -0.188 pp to -0.124 pp versus window-cropping. EMA, GlobalAmaxPool and augmentation changes gave nothing measurable to low-res robustness.
findings.relevance: Direct prior for H2.4.4's target (24/32 ratio ~0.58-0.62 with a whole-run graph, versus the arena's 0.68) and H3.2.6's condition that the curriculum pays only once overhead is gone. Fable keeps 2/3 of its epochs below 32 px, but on CIFAR-10. Treat that cautiously given E029's threshold failure at 75% low-res.

findings.claim: Fable's legitimate gain was progressive resizing (1.978 -> 1.828 s, -7.6%; ~0.15 s), plus pooling, CUDA-graph and optimizer-fusion work. Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.5 got ~23% mostly from schedule-length tuning (10.5 -> 9.0-9.75 epochs) and hyperparameter tuning. The audit flags spec gaming: precomputing augmentation outside the timed region (~0.062 s), filtering for faster hosts (~0.040 s) and a 60 s thermal cooldown (~0.009 s).
findings.relevance: Epoch-count tuning was the largest lever in the parallel CIFAR-10 effort, which is consistent with the arena's E027/E031 path. The gaming tricks are illegal here (augmentation must be in timed prepare/train; no sleeps or clock changes) and must be avoided when copying Fable ideas such as per-step augmented buffers (H2.4.4 must stage them inside timed train).

findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18704 (Exponential Moving Average of Weights in Deep Learning: Dynamics and Benefits)
findings.claim: Abstract: 'EMA requires less learning rate decay compared to SGD since averaging naturally reduces noise, introducing a form of implicit regularization'; EMA improves generalization, calibration and consistency.
findings.relevance: Supports the E035 post-mortem: averaging substitutes for annealing in a short noisy run. That favors testing stronger or tail EMA together with an LR floor instead of decay to ~0, as a margin source.

findings.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.15682 (The Road Less Scheduled); https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.03241 (Early Weight Averaging meets High LR); ICML 2025 'When, where and why to average weights' (search snippets only)

findings.relevance: Weaker, secondary support that tuning averaging (Lookahead alpha/cadence or an EMA tail) can buy accuracy at zero step cost. Not CIFAR-specific; I only saw snippets.

findings.source: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.01598v4 (Convergence Bound and Critical Batch Size of Muon Optimizer)
findings.claim: Muon has a critical batch size b* proportional to the gradient variance. Below it, steps-to-target scale inversely with batch; beyond it, larger batches yield diminishing returns. Lr and batch should be coupled as functions of total iterations.
findings.relevance: A theoretical account of E032: at batch 3072 (~140 steps) the run became step-limited. Every Muon CIFAR record found runs at batch 1536-2000, so further batch increases are unlikely to pay without retuning.

findings.claim: Gram Newton-Schulz iterates on the n×n Gram matrix XX^T instead of the n×m input. Its FLOP count is (4T+6α-6)n³, versus T(3α+1)n³ for standard NS with symmetric GEMMs (α=m/n). It needs fp16 (not bf16) and a restart after iteration 2 for stability, and the article reports 26-29% single-GPU optimizer speedups.
findings.relevance: For the arena's block-3 filters (704×6336, α≈9, T=3), the formula gives 60n³ vs 84n³, ~29% fewer NS FLOPs (my calculation). Applied to the ~0.95 ms/step bmm (E026), that is roughly 0.25 ms/step, ~0.05 s/run. Small but free at equal math if it is stable in fp16 with 3 iterations; the article did not validate that.

findings.claim: AOL diagonal preconditioning (X·diag(row-sums of |XᵀX|)^-1/2) lets Muon drop one NS iteration. On a CIFAR-10 airbench speedrun it went from 1.359 s / 94.04% to 1.348 s / 94.03%, only a 0.8% time saving.
findings.relevance: Low-value lever: shaving NS iterations has a measured ~1% ceiling on an airbench-class net.

findings.claim: airbench96 on CIFAR-100 reaches 79.27% without cutout and 79.76% with it (with TTA, long schedule). CIFAR-10 ablations: identity init 8.0 -> 6.8 s, bias scaling 64x 6.8 -> 5.1 s, Lookahead 5.1 -> 4.6 s, multi-crop TTA 4.6 -> 4.2 s. Speedups accumulate roughly additively.
findings.relevance: Confirms bias scaling as the largest post-whitening lever (H4.5 asks to verify bias_scaler 64 is present) and Lookahead as a ~10% lever, consistent with E035. The ~79% ceiling supports H5.1's wide-net ceiling.

findings.relevance: The arena tip (E031, 5.43 s) already beats the best public CIFAR-100 time, and its Muon gain (E025 +0.78 pp) contradicts PR #3's finding. There is no external CIFAR-100 recipe to copy, so remaining gains must come from transferring CIFAR-10 lineage ideas (EMA tail, 0.2-ep whiten bias, Muon lr ~0.2, color jitter, whole-run graph).
